clue.text: Ayesha taken in by raven's call from the tree

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a raven's cry is a caw
Ayesha is the title character of H. Rider Haggard's novel She, so Ayesha gives SHE

explanation.surface: A woman named Ayesha is lured by a raven calling from up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayesha is 'She-who-must-be-obeyed', heroine of H. Rider Haggard's novel She; 'taken in by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a tropical tree grown for its kidney-shaped nuts.

clue.text: You won't be able to keep your hair on when you get this complaint

definitions.text: You won't be able to keep your hair on when you get this complaint

parts.words: You won't be able to keep your hair on when you get this complaint
parts.note: keep your hair on is British slang for stay calm, but here it is literal: a condition that makes hair fall out

explanation.surface: Someone with a grievance is bound to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep your hair on' is British for 'calm down', and 'complaint' looks like a grievance but means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is the medical term for baldness or patchy hair loss.

clue.text: Sound female worker, not off the assembly line

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for the female worker is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a handmaid is a female servant

explanation.surface: A healthy woman employee who does not work in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy' but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods crafted by hand rather than mass-produced in a factory.

clue.text: Unable to stand several days on call, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken aloud and then spelt as another word

parts.note: several days is a week, and being on call is being available when needed, giving week need

explanation.surface: A doctor exhausted after being on call for days on end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the homophone: 'week need' is spoken and entered as the hyphenated word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with wobbly knees can barely keep upright; the word also means feeble or cowardly.

clue.text: Quarrelled — and possessed the vocabulary for it!

explanation.surface: Two people argued, and fittingly had the language to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words is an idiom for arguing; read literally, it means owning a stock of vocabulary.

clue.text: England v France — the LP record

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture with a famous long-playing album.
explanation.walkthrough: LP means long-playing: this Anglo-French conflict ran from 1337 to 1453, a record length.
explanation.definitionFit: The long medieval conflict between the English and French crowns, which famously lasted 116 years.

clue.text: Drinking bout occurred on ship

parts.note: occurred means was, as in it was yesterday
a sail is an old term for a ship, as in a fleet of ten sail

explanation.surface: A heavy session of drinking happened aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassail is a festive carousing session, especially with spiced ale at Christmas.

clue.text: Listen, is this not Grannie? No, certainly not

definitions.text: Listen, is this not Grannie? No, certainly not

parts.words: Listen, is this not Grannie? No, certainly not
parts.note: a granny is a badly tied version of the sailor's square knot, so the correctly tied one is certainly not a granny

explanation.surface: A family argument about whether someone is really Grandma.
explanation.walkthrough: A granny knot is the faulty, slipping version of the square knot, so 'Grannie' is a knot, not a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: The square knot used to tie two ropes, which a misplaced cross turns into a granny.

clue.text: The team pin-up is an addition to the board

parts.note: a side is a sports team
a dish is slang for a good-looking person, a pin-up

explanation.surface: The squad's glamorous poster model joins the company directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a company board but means a dining table, as in board and lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra dish served alongside the main course at the table.

clue.text: Origin of the jet

explanation.surface: A question about where a jet comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountainhead or source is an origin, and an ornamental fountain throws up a jet of water.

clue.text: Move up in progressive dances

indicators.note: progressive dances move partners along, hinting that the letters of the word dances shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Climbing the social ladder through progressive dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progressive' looks like a kind of dance but signals that DANCES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb or rise, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: College servant who creates litter

parts.note: a litter is also an old word for a bed, so a college servant who makes the students' beds is the one creating litter

explanation.surface: A college porter who leaves rubbish lying about.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a bedmaker is the servant who tidies students' rooms; 'litter' is used in its sense of bedding, not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The college staff member who tidies rooms and makes the beds; litter is straw bedding.

clue.text: Identified patent

explanation.surface: Something recognised and plainly evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked can mean singled out or labelled, and also obvious or conspicuous, as patent does.

clue.text: Defraud Liberal constituents how shocking!

indicators.note: the constituents of something are its parts, here the letters taken apart and rebuilt

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: Outrage that a Liberal politician cheated the voters in his own constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters but signals the anagram of DEFRAUD plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful! is an exclamation of horror, matching an outraged cry of disapproval.

clue.text: A French female on a mountain in Africa can't be got down

parts.note: une is the French word for a used with a feminine noun
Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town in South Africa

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman stuck on an African peak who cannot get down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got down' looks like descending but means swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be swallowed is inedible.

clue.text: Support for evil

explanation.surface: Backing for wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A base is a foundation that holds something up; base also means morally low or wicked.

clue.text: Boycott international singer

parts.note: to black a firm or goods is to boycott them
a cap is awarded to a player chosen for their national team, so an international is a cap

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the England cricketer, as a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott is a famous England cricketer, so the surface points to a person; 'singer' is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackcap is a warbler with a fine song, and birds are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Sort of clues he'd have a timetable for

indicators.note: to sort something is to rearrange it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A setter planning when to produce certain clues.
explanation.definitionFit: To schedule an event is to fix it in a timetable.

clue.text: Cut out wretched centre spread

indicators.note: the centre spread of a word is its middle stretch of letters, the outer two at each end dropped

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor ditches a miserable centrefold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre spread' looks like the middle pages of a magazine but picks the central letters of 'wretched'.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave, cutting a design into a surface with acid or a tool.

clue.text: Shell makes about everybody inside sit up

indicators.note: inside means these pieces go within the other
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to pose is to sit for a portrait
C is the abbreviation of circa, about
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A seashell that makes everyone sit up and take notice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading backwards; 'inside' places the abbreviation for about plus everybody within the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: An escallop is a scallop, a bivalve mollusc, or its fan-shaped shell.

clue.text: Each land in the melting pot of Babylonia

indicators.note: something in the melting pot is being remade, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Every country in the cultural mix of ancient Babylon.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaldea was a region of southern Mesopotamia, and the term came to mean Babylonian.

clue.text: Leisure wherein love finds heart's-ease

explanation.surface: Free time is where romance discovers a pansy.
explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-idleness and heartsease are both old names for the wild pansy, so love is found 'in' this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is time free from work, and the flower love-in-idleness is also called heartsease.

clue.text: This kind of selling is no go

explanation.surface: A sales technique that gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Inertia selling sends goods unasked and bills those who fail to return them.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia selling relies on customers not acting; physical inertia is a reluctance to move.

clue.text: Skilful Conservative means of exerting pressure

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to apply force

explanation.surface: An adept Tory knows how to apply leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever means quick-witted and able, as skilful does.

clue.text: Regard island retreat as subject to local taxation

parts.note: to rate something is to regard or value it

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the island's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Viewing an island hideaway as liable for council tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a holiday hideaway but turns ELBA into ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: British local taxes were called rates, so property liable to them was rateable.

clue.text: Bucks, for example, with social pretensions

explanation.surface: Young men about town who put on airs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county; 'county' also describes the snobbish landed gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckinghamshire is a shire; as an adjective the word describes upper-class rural gentry manners.

clue.text: US workers 'of the world — no, not the Shakers

definitions.text: US workers 'of the world — no, not the Shakers

parts.words: US workers 'of the world — no, not the Shakers
parts.note: members of the Industrial Workers of the World union have a nickname suggesting shakiness, yet they are not the religious sect known as Shakers

explanation.surface: Clarifying which American labour movement is meant: not the religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Industrial Workers of the World is an American radical union; its members' nickname sounds like trembling, hence the joke about Shakers, a US religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Industrial Workers of the World, a US labour union, carry this nickname.

clue.text: Disturbing report about US lawyer — he feeds off others

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
disturbing something jumbles it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: DA, district attorney, is a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: An alarming account of an American lawyer who lives off other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' looks like an adjective describing the report, but it is the anagram signal; 'about' wraps the shuffled letters round the American prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator is an animal that hunts and eats other creatures.

clue.text: Become genial to swell

explanation.surface: Grow friendlier and grow bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand can mean to open up and become talkative, and also to grow larger.
